title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The incident title describes a lawyer in Minnesota being suspended for submitting fake case citations generated by an AI system. This is a known failure mode in which a language model asserts fabricated legal citations as fact, producing case names, docket numbers, or holdings that do not exist in any court record. The failure occurs at the point of use, when a practitioner relies on AI-generated text without independently verifying each citation against an authoritative legal database before filing.

Catching this failure requires only that a human check each cited case against an actual legal record before submitting a document to a court. No specialized tool is needed, because bar associations and courts have long required attorneys to verify the accuracy of their filings through standard legal research.

The actual article content was not available to the reporting source used here, so the specific AI system involved, the number of fabricated citations, and the precise terms of the suspension are not established by the facts provided.
